perspective:
Cynthia’s accessible information:

- Cynthia teaches evening classes at the community center. Christina is her colleague and manages marketing there. They have a professional working relationship that has sometimes involved clashes over program/marketing direction.
- At the staff meeting, Cynthia argues that the next campaign should highlight traditional classes because they are the backbone of past success, have proven worth over time, and appeal to long-time/core attendees. She worries that shifting focus too much could alienate them.
- Cynthia hears Christina respond that she understands Cynthia’s point but wants to showcase more dynamic, interactive sessions; Christina says it is about enhancing offerings and finding balance, not replacing what works. Cynthia remains unconvinced at that point.
- Cynthia witnesses positive feedback from Christina’s new, innovative marketing campaign. She asks Christina what she did differently.
- Christina tells Cynthia she focused on interactive elements and social media to create conversation rather than just broadcast information. Christina also says blending the new with the old means they can learn from each other.
- Cynthia finds this intriguing and says Christina managed to capture both depth and flash.
- Encouraged by this new understanding, Cynthia proposes a joint pilot project combining traditional lectures with interactive online sessions. Christina likes the idea and agrees to outline specifics.
- Cynthia hopes the project will enhance learning and draw a wider audience.
- The pilot project succeeds. Cynthia tells Christina they should scale it up immediately and says she will organize resources and set up a schedule.
- Christina says she will coordinate with the marketing team to spread the word. Cynthia says she is excited and expects a big impact.
- After the blended methods are implemented, Cynthia prepares a presentation to showcase the project’s success and advocate expanding it to other centers.
- Cynthia tells Christina the feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. Christina offers help and agrees other centers could benefit.
- Cynthia feels proud of what they achieved and sees it as proof that blending their methods was the right move.

Excluded from Cynthia’s perspective: private facts about Christina such as her personality type, education, ethnicity, internal motives, and any events or narrator-only information Cynthia did not observe or was not told.
